claims: n292/n292_exact.json states 292 unit squares as centre and unit edge direction rows of exact rationals, with the side 33872522175917279266554668306659248043633029180856810473/1925667453806884053962316529711800854170000000000000000; #1006 and the root README round it up at 12 places as 17.590016442847, and n292/README.md prints 17.5900164428464147126481796, rounded up at 25 places. n292/n292_witness.yaml states the same packing as a packing.squares:Witness/v2 document of rational corners. #1006 names the record's 17.5913781454976982 at 292 (T-146) at jlevy/squares f9ddfeeef and the gain on it, 0.00136, and says later commits leave these files unchanged.

n292/README.md and #1006 say the packing has one continuous ribbon of 59 squares tilted by 40 to 42 degrees along the diagonal and 233 axis-aligned squares in the two triangular regions beside it; the ribbon extends the 37-square tilted ribbon of the packing of 146 squares with side 12.583782190152 that the record credits to David W. Cantrell (2025), which repeats after a shift of (5, 5), two copies at (0, 0) and (5, 5) sharing 15 squares; the coordinates of that packing were taken from a public Kaggle notebook (sigmaborov, 'Squares in Squares: certified contact polish', Apache License 2.0, as included in areebbb's 'merge 28' notebook); an integer program placed the axis-aligned squares, a numerical optimization of all 292 squares followed, and the result was rounded to exact rational coordinates; the record's packing at 292 has two separate tilted blocks of 16 and 33 squares. They say a linear program over all 292 squares, with every contact linearized, found no first-order improvement, a test of one set of contacts; that the certificate keeps a smallest gap of 3e-12, so an exact solution of the contact equations would be smaller by an amount of that order; that no local or global optimality is proved; and that a table of the Kaggle competition's best sides per team (Samanyu-dev/squares_in_squares, 8 November 2026) lists 17.589053943368 at 292 for the team 'Cats and boxes', with no public packing, and a public merged submission (bestbryant/claude_code_squaresinsquares, 16 November 2026) lists 17.591378147172. #1006 asks that the bound be credited to Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology, as an extension of Cantrell's ribbon.

verify_exact.py (separating axes) and check_area.py (the area of each close pair's clipped intersection), both Python's fractions.Fraction and its standard library only, are the folder's two exact checkers; #1006 says each reports 292 squares and 668 close pairs, that this repository's check_rational_witness_independent.py reports 'VERIFIED: 292 squares, 42486 pairs' on the witness, and that the witness validates against this repository's witness.schema.yaml with 0 errors; it says the first two share no code but have one author and read the same input file. #1006 says the construction and the search were run with Gemini Carbon (Google), and the checking, the witness file, the figure and the comparison with other known values were produced with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), both under his direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
